question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to the core agent loop, and must that mode wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is real, but the fix changes core runtime scheduling and safety semantics rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design opt-in core mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for owner design covering early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block on safety metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on a concurrency-safety tool contract such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 before runtime scheduling work starts.

options.title: Keep post-stream batching only
options.body: Leave current behavior as the supported default if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for the core runtime right now.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for owner design covering early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.
